slides.title: Linear and Affine Connections
slides.notes: Open by positioning the chapter as a bridge between the principal-bundle language of Chapter 2 and the concrete geometry students expect on the tangent bundle. The lecture will keep two pictures synchronized: horizontal motion upstairs in frame bundles and visible consequences downstairs as covariant derivatives, geodesics, and holonomy.

slides.title: Route Through The Chapter
slides.notes: Use this route slide to prevent the lecture from becoming a dictionary. The source span has many propositions, but the organizing chain is simple: define horizontal transport, express it with forms, measure its failures through torsion and curvature, then recover familiar coordinates and geodesic tools.

slides.title: Connections In A Vector Bundle
slides.notes: Emphasize that the derivative is not obtained by subtracting vectors in unrelated fibers. A connection supplies the comparison rule first, and only then does the Leibniz formula make sense. This is the vector-bundle version of the horizontal-lift story already built for principal bundles.

slides.title: Parallel Transport And A Bundle Metric
slides.notes: The chapter proves existence results for connections and then singles out metric-preserving behavior as a useful refinement. Present this as a design choice: many connections differentiate sections, but a metric-compatible one also promises that parallel transport does not distort fiber lengths or pairings.

slides.title: The Frame Bundle Encodes Linear Connections
slides.notes: Move students from the abstract phrase linear connection to a concrete bookkeeping device. A point of the frame bundle is a choice of basis in a tangent space. The connection form detects how that basis changes vertically, while the solder form remembers the base velocity written in that basis.

slides.title: Structure Equations
slides.notes: Treat the equations as diagnostics, not as formal decorations. The solder form turns base motion into vector components, so its derivative exposes torsion. The connection form records frame change, so its derivative and bracket term expose curvature. This is the algebraic heart of the chapter.

slides.title: Bianchi Identities As Consistency Checks
slides.notes: Students often memorize Bianchi identities after seeing them in Riemannian geometry, but here they arise directly from the frame-bundle structure equations. Explain them as compatibility audits: once torsion and curvature are produced by a single connection, their covariant derivatives must satisfy these linked constraints.

slides.title: Covariant Derivatives Of Tensor Fields
slides.notes: This slide is the algebraic payoff of the earlier definitions. Once the connection differentiates vector fields and covectors, the product rule and contraction rule determine its behavior on all tensors. Parallel tensor fields then become invariant objects transported unchanged by the connection.

slides.title: From Linear To Affine Connections
slides.notes: Make the affine step geometrically concrete. A linear frame knows how to compare directions; an affine frame also remembers where the origin of the model space has been placed. The chapter relates these by projecting affine information back to the linear frame bundle.

slides.title: Development Of A Curve
slides.notes: Development is the lecture's most visual construction. The curve is not copied into Euclidean space by coordinates; it is rolled out using horizontal frames. This is why the result detects the connection itself. A straight developed curve is the clean signature of a geodesic.

slides.title: Torsion And Curvature Tensors
slides.notes: Distinguish the two failures carefully. Torsion compares the skew part of covariant differentiation with the actual Lie bracket of vector fields. Curvature compares the two orders of second covariant differentiation. Both are tensors, so their values can be checked at a point using convenient extensions.

slides.title: Bianchi Identities With Torsion
slides.notes: When torsion is present, the familiar Riemannian identities acquire correction terms. Do not let the notation hide the idea: the cyclic sum is comparing three ways to travel around an infinitesimal triangle. Torsion contributes because the triangle itself fails to close in the naive way.

slides.title: Geodesics As Horizontal Dynamics
slides.notes: Frame geodesics as dynamics determined by the connection, not as shortest paths. A curve is geodesic when its velocity is transported parallel to itself. The development criterion gives students an immediate visual test: under the chosen connection, the curve rolls out to a straight line.

slides.title: Coordinate Expressions
slides.notes: Coordinates are useful but dangerous. The Christoffel symbols are the local coefficients of a connection, not tensor components by themselves. Torsion and curvature are built from them in combinations that transform tensorially, while the geodesic equation exposes the ordinary differential equation behind autoparallel curves.

slides.title: Normal Coordinates
slides.notes: Explain normal coordinates as a way to spend geodesics as coordinates. The exponential map sends tangent vectors to points reached by geodesics, so radial lines become geodesic paths. In the torsion-free case, the first-order Christoffel data can be erased at the base point.

slides.title: Linear Infinitesimal Holonomy
slides.notes: Connect this section back to Chapter 2 without assuming the audience remembers every holonomy theorem. Holonomy is what parallel transport can do around loops. Infinitesimally, the algebra is generated by curvature and its covariant derivatives, so curvature is not only a defect but a generator.

slides.title: Notebook Lab: Three Inspections
slides.notes: Tie the deck back to the assigned notebook. The notebook is deliberately small, but it models a useful habit: turn definitions into data, turn theorems into dependency checks, and make every formula answer an inspection question. This prevents the chapter from becoming pure notation.

slides.title: Closing Checklist
slides.notes: Close by giving students a portable reading protocol. For any connection question, they should identify the bundle, the horizontal rule, the induced transport, and the diagnostic tensor. This checklist will be reused immediately when the course specializes to Riemannian metrics and Levi-Civita connections.
